title: Amy Poehler on Her Ghost Hunter SNL Sketch with DIG Costar Hugh Laurie: "He's So..."
excerpt: Amy Poehler recalls her hilarious 2006 SNL sketch with Hugh Laurie and shares how her former co-star helped her on Peacock’s DIG.
content:
Amy Poehler's history with DIG co-star Hugh Laurie dates back to 2006 — more than 20 years before the series premiere of their new Peacock comedy.

During Poehler's November 18 visit to Late Night with Seth Meyers, the Saturday Night Live alum reminisced about the times her DIG castmate hosted the show while both Poehler and Seth Meyers were cast members. Meyers specifically asked Poehler about Season 32's "Most Haunted," a parody the popular Travel Channel investigative series.

Poehler also noted that before American audiences knew Laurie as a grouchy doctor on TV's House, "we knew Hugh as a sketch artist earlier," in a nod to his early-career roots in the genre.

RELATED: Everything to Know About DIG, Amy Poehler's New Peacock Show Co-Created By Mike Schur

Amy Poehler & Hugh Laurie starred in the 2006 SNL ghost hunter sketch "Most Haunted"

"Most Haunted" stars Laurie as ghost hunter Derek Acorah who leads his team (Season 32 cast members Poehler, Fred Armisen, and Bill Hader) into a mysterious home in search of otherworldy spirits. While the group doesn't find ghosts, their tools do detect mysterious flatulence.

"Basically, people kept farting," Meyers recalled.

"There was a ghost that farted," Poehler added. "And it was so funny." Watch the sketch above.

"Most Haunted" originally aired on October 28, 2006. Meyers credited longtime SNL writer James Anderson as the mind behind it. During his 20-year tenure as a writer from 2000 to 2020, Anderson's body of work includes the Target Lady sketches with Kristen Wiig, "Westminster Daddy Show" and "The Californians."

RELATED: SNL's "Sister" Sketch Is Hitting Home for Family Caregivers Who Do Everything

Hugh Laurie starred in sketch comedy series A Bit of Fry and Laurie

Laurie hosted SNL twice, in Season 32 on October 28, 2006 and in Season 34 on December 13, 2008. Laurie's second appearance coincided with Poehler's final episode as a cast member. 

"We knew Hugh as a sketch artist earlier, before people knew him as a serious dramatic actor doing an American accent, but he's so funny," she told Meyers.

While attending Cambridge University in England, Laurie met his soon-to-be longtime collaborator, Stephen Fry, as the two were part of Cambridge Footlights troupe. Both went on to do character work in British live comedy and music series Saturday Live — not to be confused with today's Saturday Night Live UK — and 1987, the duo starred in popular BBC sketch series A Bit of Fry & Laurie for 26 episodes across four seasons.

RELATED: How to Watch A Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving Ahead of Turkey Day in 2026

Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie star in Peacock’s new show DIG

All ten episodes of Poehler's new comedy, DIG, premiere Monday, November 23, 2026 exclusively on Peacock. Laurie plays her character's boss Neville, and you can watch the trailer here.

The show marks Poehler's first foray into network comedy since Parks and Recreation, which ran on NBC from 2009 to 2015. The star admitted to Meyers that it was "hard" to get back into acting when filming for DIG kicked off, and credited Laurie for helping her stay locked in.

"I was rusty, and I was working with Hugh, who's so good. And it did definitely feel like starting at the top of the mountain," Poehler revealed.

"By the way, the pilot's fantastic and the cast is great and you are not rusty at all," Meyers assured her.

"Thanks a lot. We used a lot of AI! Just kidding," Poehler quipped.
